Oliver found this star in the dry riverbed. It vibrated three times, like the bell he had not yet heard.
The tower was missing its final chime. The clapper had fallen into the river; the silence seemed to await a small hand.
Three bridges, two banks, a forgotten path. On Oliver's map, the star marked the bridge nobody remembered.
The old guardian's compass opened the map and broke. One tip pointed to the tower; the other to the river.
Oliver crossed the bridge without counting his steps. Beneath the golden arch, he heard the lost chime follow the current.
On the other bank, a seed held the star's light. Oliver planted it where the water still remembered the bell's sound.
The lantern stayed lit until the last star. The little glass tree leaned its branches toward the harbor.
A paper boat carried the clapper. Whoever folded it left just three marks: the same ones missing from the map.
Back at the tower, Oliver returned the clapper. The third chime came not from the bell, but from the star in his hand.
The repaired compass rests in the workshop. At night, the glass tree chimes softly. A fourth mark is appearing on the map.
The bell found its third note. Oliver returned the light he held to the river: one current woke the roots, the other showed the way home. No star had to belong to him to light someone else's way.
